§6Inside the Reactor§f

§aUnderstanding the component layout.§f
A Solid Fission Reactor is made of several component types, each with a specific role:

§bFuel Cells§f: Hold the fuel and produce heat + neutrons. Place them where they can reach moderators.
§bHeat Sinks§f: Absorb heat. Each type has a cooling rate and placement rule (e.g., Water Sink needs exactly one adjacent chamber).
§bModerators§f: Redirect neutrons to adjacent fuel cells. Graphite gives +10 flux, Beryllium +22, Heavy Water +36.
§bReflectors§f: Bounce neutrons back into the reactor. Beryllium reflects 50% efficiency, Lead-Steel 25%.

The layout matters. A well-designed reactor can double or triple the output of a poorly planned one.

§ePS:§f Use a reactor planner tool to test layouts before building. Trial and error gets expensive fast.
